token_id.description: An id that is one NATS subject token. Ids starting with an underscore are reserved for the system; runtime ids starting with x- are reserved, because that sender slot names other installations.

installation_id.description: An installation: one authority and the hosts it certifies. At most 62 characters, so that x-<installation> is one subject token.

team_id.description: A team: one NATS subject token of at most 24 characters. A host's credential names its teams' streams and consumers once per agent it runs, so short team ids keep it within max_credential_bytes (README, "Credential size"). Ids starting with an underscore are reserved.

runtime_id.description: One runtime host: a supervisor process that runs agent sessions. Unique within an installation.

agent_id.description: An agent's stable id: one NATS subject token of at most 32 characters, which a host's credential names in each of the agent's grants (README, "Credential size"). It stays the same when the agent restarts or moves to another host.

durable_owner_id.description: The stored owner of an Objective or its work records, including manager_scope:<team>:<role>. This is data, never a routing or certificate agent id.

agent_type.description: A kind of agent, which also names its worker pool: one NATS subject token of at most 24 characters, which a host's credential names in each pool's grants (README, "Credential size").

session_id.description: One run of an agent on one host, named by its agent session certificate. A restart or a move starts a new session.

record_id.description: An id that names a task, command, question or other record. It may hold colons and dots, so it is never used as a subject token.

message_id.description: A UUIDv7 in lower-case text form.

idempotency_key.description: The sender's key for one logical send: the kind, a colon, and the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 array of the values the registry names (README, "Idempotency keys"). The same key always means the same message.

kind.description: A message kind or operation name: lower-case words joined by dots. At most 84 characters, so an idempotency key (the kind, a colon and 43 digest characters) stays within 128.

timestamp.description: A UTC time from 1970 to 9999 with exactly three fractional digits. Receivers also refuse dates that do not exist, such as 30 February.

sha256_digest.description: A SHA-256 digest in unpadded base64url.

ed25519_signature.description: An Ed25519 signature in unpadded base64url.

ed25519_public_key.description: An Ed25519 public key in unpadded base64url.

person_ref.description: An opaque reference to a person. It never holds a channel address, name or account id.

delivery_ref.description: An opaque reference to where a person is reached, which only the gateway can resolve: dr_ and at least 16 random characters, so a phone number, chat id or handle can never pass as one.

blob_ref.description: A file or long text in the object store, named by its digest.

issuer.description: Who signed the frame: the host, by its certificate, and the agent session it signed for. Receivers look the certificate and the session up in their trust store; nothing here is trusted until those records confirm it.

audience.description: Who the frame is for. Agents are named by id, never by the host that runs them. Broadcast events name their whole team (target team, id the team id); team services also use the team id. A reply to a request a host sent for no agent (sessions.*) names the host: target host, id and runtime its runtime id. No request is delivered to a host target.

authority_token.description: Proof that work acts for a person, issued by a gateway or scheduler host and bound to one root task, one command or one access request. It names the team the person asked (its audience), and only that team presents it, copied unchanged down a delegation tree. System work, which a schedule runs for no person, carries a scheduler's token that names its schedule and no person. The token names no roles: receivers read the person's current roles and standing from the team's people records. The signature covers the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the token without its signature, after the domain prefix universal-agents/authority-token/v1 and a newline.

issuer.description: The gateway or scheduler host that signed the token, by its certificate.

audience.description: The team the person asked; only that team presents the token. Its installation is the issuer's.

person.description: The person the work is for. Absent only in system work: a scheduler's token that names its schedule_id (README, "On behalf of a person").

schedule_id.description: The schedule a scheduled job's run belongs to. Only a scheduler certificate signs it, and a run's schedule comes only from here (README, "On behalf of a person").

host_role.description: A host role from the registry's host_roles.

agent_role.description: An agent's place in its team, from team-topologies.yaml.

application_key.description: A host's or authority's Ed25519 signing key and the id that frames and records name it by.

state_key.description: A key-value key: one to four tokens joined by dots.

state_writer.description: Who signed a state record: an installation's authority key, or a host by its certificate.

state_sequence.description: The writer's counter for this key; readers keep the record with the highest one.

tool_list.description: The catalog tools a host can run: what an administrator approved with its join (README, "Access on remote hosts"). Readers refuse a list that names a tool twice.

action_digest.description: The digest of one exact action, which a one-time approval is bound to.

custody_token.description: The custody record's revision. A holder learns it from custody.confirmed, which the team services send when they record its claim or a reassignment to it.

connection_class.description: How a host is connected, approved with its join and named in its certificate: connected hosts (the main machine, servers) are expected to stay connected; intermittent hosts (edge devices, laptops) are expected to be cut off for long stretches. It decides the kind of custody window its holders get (README, "Custody windows").

custody_window.description: How long a holder's custody lasts without a new confirmation (README, "Custody windows"). Its kind matches the holder's host certificate: host_record for a connected host, reconnection for an intermittent one.

oneOf.description: A connected host's window: it lasts this many seconds after the holder's last host record write that the store acknowledged, so every host record write renews it. Standard: 300.

An intermittent host's window: it ends at a fixed time, standard 5 days after the confirmation and never more than 7 days after the frame that carries it was issued. Only a new custody.confirmed renews it, which the team services send when the host reconnects.

task_access_list.description: What one task may use on a host whose certificate names its tools, worked out by the team services with the same access decision as on the main machine and carried in their signed frame (README, "Access on remote hosts"). The holder keeps the list with the highest sequence for its task.

sequence.description: Rises with each new list for the task.

root_task_id.description: The person's request the task belongs to: the root task its authority token is bound to.

person.description: The person the work is for. Absent only in system work, whose token names a schedule and no person.

ends_at.description: When the list stops counting: the task's end, at most 7 days after issued_at.

fresh_check.description: The tool runs only with a block list at most 15 minutes old (block_list fresh_seconds); by default tools that spend money or publish as the person.

one_time.description: Approvals for one exact action each. The host uses each once and records the use durably before the action.

contract_sha256.description: The contract digest of the compatibility record (README, "Versions"): lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256.

resource_key.description: Something a person's requests may both change, which coordination claims, checks, notes and waits name (README, "Coordination between a person's requests"). The host's trusted code builds it from what the agent named; it is never free text. file:<folder target>, with the folder target grammar of access grants (team/..., agents/..., users/<folder>/... or data/<name>/...; no empty, . or .. part, no backslash and no control character): a folder always ends with a slash, a top folder too (file:team/), and covers everything under it; a file never does. record:<kind>:<id> for a knowledge page (record:knowledge_page:<space>:<page>), a memory fact (record:memory_fact:<bank>:<number>), a schedule, an Objective or a heartbeat item. account:<tool>:<owner> for the team's or the person's account of a tool. A key in a person's own space (a personal page, a usermem fact, the person's account) names the token person's own record.

coordination_request_title.description: A request's title: its thread's subject preview, or its schedule's or Objective's name.

coordination_claim.description: One of the asking person's claims, as its own requests see it.

coordination_note.description: A note one of the asking person's requests left.

coordination_holder.description: Whose claim it is. The asking person's own requests are described in full; another person's request only as "another team member's request"; work for no person is team maintenance, the team's own work, whose reason every request sees.

coordination_seen_claim.description: A live claim on, above or under a resource.

relation.description: Where the claimed resource sits: the resource asked about, a folder above it, or something under it.

coordination_own_seen_claim.description: One of the asking request's own live claims on, above or under a resource it asked about, as shared_work.claim lists its own (holder this_request), so the model sees which claim to use, extend or release.

relation.description: Where the claimed resource sits: the resource asked about, a folder above it, or something under it.

coordination_seen_note.description: A note left on a resource. Another person's note shows only that one exists; team maintenance's shows its text to every request.

coordination_event.description: Something that happened to a task's coordination that its requester may need to plan around; trusted code adds it, at most one event of each kind, each listing up to eight cases with how many there were (README, "Coordination between a person's requests").

total.description: How many times it happened, at least as many as listed.
How many times it happened, at least as many as listed.
How many times it happened, at least as many as listed.
How many times it happened, at least as many as listed.
How many times it happened, at least as many as listed.
How many times it happened, at least as many as listed.

attachment.description: A file sent with a message, held in the object store.

replied_message.description: The message the person replied to.

assumption.description: Something the work relied on that later steering may change.

held_action.description: An outward action and how far it got.

decision_ahead.description: A decision the lead made in advance for one task or schedule.

credential_field_kind.description: What a credential field holds. The broker treats password, token, api_key, secret, totp and credential_file as secret whatever the field's visibility.

credential_visible_kind.description: The field kinds whose value may be shown to agents: never a secret.

broker_session_id.description: The secure broker's form session: its unpadded base64url random id.

answer.description: A task's answer: text, or a text file in the object store when it is longer than long_text allows. A result passed on as it is carries the subtask's answer itself, copied by code, and names the subtask.

access_ask.description: What an access request asks for: access to one target, approval of a staged change, or the person's review of a change another writer made to a record this task wants to change.

oneOf.description: A change review: the store refused this task's change because another writer changed the record (change_conflict or needs_person_decision), and the holder asks the person the request works for (README, "Change reviews").

case_id.description: The case the store's refusal named.

question.description: The agent's question to the person, in its own words.

recipient.description: Whom a notice or review is for: the person behind a delivery reference, or the team's administrators.

reply_target.description: Where a task's results, questions, progress, claims and reports go: its requester. A delegation names the delegating agent; a task the gateway starts for a person, or a run of a person's own schedule, names the gateway route that reaches the person (README, "Replies").

work_context.description: Where a task sits in its request and how it should run.

delivery_mode.description: How the gateway delivers to the person: an interactive reply, a scheduled (cron) or deferred message, a heartbeat, or one of the system schedules' modes.

ledger_snapshot.description: A task's open work, carried by a handback so its new holder keeps the same labels.

record_version.description: The version of a stored record that a writer saw, as the store reports it.

schedule_action.description: What each run of a schedule does, with schedules.install's action types: task gives the instruction to a model turn; fixed_message sends the text as it is, without a model turn.

text_content.description: UTF-8 plain text, inline or held in the object store. Use a blob when the whole serialized frame would exceed its size limit.

person.description: The person, by reference. Absent when the team's people records no longer hold them, such as someone who left the team.

knowledge_note.description: An open note whose id can be passed to knowledge.resolve_note.

scope_id.description: A team (at most 24 characters, as team_id), or _install for installation-wide traffic.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the certificate record's signing bytes (its domain prefix and canonical JSON without the signature), as TrustStore.add records it.

certificate_ref.description: A host certificate record: its id, membership epoch and digest.

connection_credential.description: The credential a host connects to NATS with, naming the agents and pools it runs; it ends no later than the certificate it comes with. Never logged.

jwt.description: At most transport.yaml max_credential_bytes: the generator keeps the two equal.

coordination_resource_notes.description: The notes on one resource, newest first.

notes_total.description: How many notes there are on it in all.

coordination_wait_target.description: What a wait of the asking person's work is for: a resource, or another of the person's requests.

coordination_own_wait.description: One of the asking request's own waits.

busy_claim.description: The claim that made a covered change wait (README, "Covered changes"): its id and resource, when it ends, whose kind of request holds it, and how many notes are on the resource. The host reads the holder's description and the notes with shared_work.check when it shows the refusal to the model.

whose.description: Another of the person's own requests, another team member's request, or team maintenance. A request's own claims never refuse its writes.
